summary: Scripting Bridge drives other apps by sending Apple events to their sdef-described scripting interface, with generated Objective-C proxies. BifrOSt has no Apple-event or sdef layer and no generated proxies. Its nearest counterpart is a per-app JSON-RPC control socket that only the same user can reach, plus a workspace API for launching and watching apps. Apps can read and call each other's named methods, but there is no generic property and element model.

features.feature: Attach to a running scriptable app (SBApplication init by bundle id, pid or URL)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/workspace.rs (running_applications, frontmost_application, url_for_application), springboard/sdk/src/control.rs (per-app socket), springboard/sdk/src/script_target.rs (attach, socket_path)
features.note: attach resolves a bundle id, process id or bundle URL against a running-app list (first match wins, trailing slashes ignored) and socket_path gives the per-app control socket; both are tested headless in springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-29.rs. Gap: the shell's running list carries only app ids, so attaching by process id or URL needs the shell to report those, and there is no handle object that sends calls to the attached app; the live check needs the lab machine.

features.feature: Launch and activate a target app
features.note: open_with starts an installed app by id. Launch flags and an explicit activate call are not exposed. workspace.rs states that nothing there launches a binary.

features.feature: Scripting class mapping from a dictionary (sdef) to generated proxies
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 1 (parity/integration 0d0412c3): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No machine-readable dictionary and no generated client classes. Each app lists its methods at runtime (app.methods).

features.feature: Properties and elements (get, set, property(withCode:), elementArray(withCode:))
features.apple: SBObject property(withCode:), property(with:code:), elementArray(withCode:), setTo(_:), get()
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/control.rs (method dispatch via handle(method, params)); springboard/apps/notes-desktop/CHANGELOG.md (notes.list, notes.get)
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 8 tests. Apps expose named read methods, such as notes.list and notes.get. Nothing here sets properties. No generic object graph exists, and no property code is addressed through a shared model.

features.feature: Element arrays with lookup by name, id or index, and per-element filtering
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/intents.rs (EntityQuery: entity.query with suggested, ids or string)
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 32 tests. Typed entity queries cover ids and text search through App::entities. There is no generic array type and no per-element message mapping.

features.feature: Error reporting per object and per application (lastError, eventDidFail delegate)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/control.rs (RpcError::new, with_reason, JSON-RPC error reply in handle_line)
features.note: verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 8 tests. Callers get a typed error code, message and reason for each call. The last-error state and the failure callback are not offered, so a caller cannot ask an object for its last error.
verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 8 tests. A handler can defer its reply and set a timeout on the pending call. There is no per-app send mode setting and no equivalent of the Apple event send modes.

features.apple: Apple event descriptors bridged to Cocoa objects through the Scripting Bridge runtime
features.bifrost: none; the wire format is JSON-RPC 2.0 over an owner-only Unix socket (springboard/sdk/src/control.rs, SO_PEERCRED check)
features.note: Apple events and OSA are Apple-only transports with no equivalent here. The JSON-RPC socket covers the same job of controlling one app from another.

gaps: Scripting dictionaries are declared in manifest.toml ([[script.command]], [[script.class]]), not as sdef files, and there are no generated client proxies; the tell-block language resolves commands through them (springboard/core/src/script/dictionary.rs).
No generic property and element model: apps cannot set properties through a shared API, and element lookup is limited to typed entity queries.
No per-object or per-application last-error state and no failure delegate for callers.
The control socket accepts only the owning user (SO_PEERCRED), so one app cannot script another app that runs under a different account.
No explicit activate or launch-flag options when a caller starts an app; open_with only starts an installed app by id.
